name: Tadalafil ED integrated trials
question: Does as-needed tadalafil improve erectile function compared with placebo in men with erectile dysfunction?

design.population: 1,112 men aged 22–82 years with mild to severe erectile dysfunction of varied etiologies across five trials.
design.description: Integrated analysis of five double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trials

verdictNote: All three prespecified efficacy measures favored tadalafil over placebo.
takeaway: Across five placebo-controlled trials, as-needed tadalafil improved erectile-function scores and sexual-encounter outcomes versus placebo in men with erectile dysfunction; at 20 mg, 81% reported improved erections versus 35% with placebo.

reports.label: Five-trial integrated analysis
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give October 2002, without a day
reports.citation: Brock GB, McMahon CG, Chen KK, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of Tadalafil for the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction: Results of Integrated Analyses." *J Urol.* 2002;168(4 Pt 1):1332-1336. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(05)64442-4

results.measure: Mean change from baseline, 20-mg tadalafil versus placebo
results.note: The abstract gives the tadalafil change but not the placebo change.
The abstract identifies this coprimary endpoint and says all efficacy outcomes improved significantly; it gives no endpoint-specific values.
